thread.title: Apple will drop Qualcomm, Broadcom components in next iPhones: Analyst - MarketWatch

author: Jeremy C. Owens
title: Apple will drop Qualcomm, Broadcom components in next iPhones: Analyst - MarketWatch
text: Instinet analyst Romit Shah predicted that Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.60% will dump chips made by Broadcom Ltd. AVGO, +2.97% and Qualcomm Inc. QCOM, -2.56% in the next iPhone to cut costs. The analyst expect Apple to dump Qualcomm LTE modem chips for those from Intel Corp. INTC, +1.97% which has already put some modems into iPhones in the past. "Qualcomm's modem technology is solid, but Intel modems cost less while still meeting Apple's standards," Shah wrote, adding that the move could save Apple more than $100 million. Apple and Qualcomm are in a legal battle right now about the licensing fees Qualcomm charges Apple. Shah said he expects Apple to move from Broadcom to Qorvo Inc. QRVO, -0.11% for a socket component, and Qorvo seemed to confirm new Apple business on the horizon in an earnings report last week that sent shares near record highs. In wireless charging, Shah believes Apple will drop Broadcom offerings for STMicroelectronics NV STM, +1.18% Broadcom is attempting to acquire Qualcomm, and increased its offer for the company Monday morning , but that didn't help Qualcomm share prices, which fell more than 2.5% in early trading while Broadcom shares gained more than 1%. Apple stock rebounded from a Friday post-earnings decline that sent it into correction territory , gaining more than 1% in early trading.
